name: Brian L. Roberts

career.title: Trainee in the Trenton, N.J. cable system, then line installer and branch-office roles
Head of operations / Executive Vice President
Chairman and Co-Chief Executive Officer (with Mike Cavanagh)

background_rationale: The son of Comcast's founder, he joined the family company out of Wharton as a cable-system trainee and line installer and rose through branch and operations roles to become president at 31.

notable.summary: Comcast bid for Warner Bros. Discovery's studio and streaming assets but lost to Netflix, which reached a $72 billion agreement, and said it would not pursue the company further.
Comcast completed the spin-off of most of its cable networks, including CNBC, MS NOW and USA Network, into a separately traded company, Versant Media Group.

Comcast announced plans to split into two public companies, spinning off NBCUniversal and Sky from its connectivity business within about a year, with Roberts to remain chairman and stay involved in leading both.
Announcing the split, Roberts said the transaction "will unlock a more entrepreneurial management approach and open up a multitude of new opportunities for each business."

personal_story.hook: Comcast's founder sent his son to Trenton as a cable trainee; at 31, Brian Roberts was the company's president.
personal_story.summary: Roberts was born in Philadelphia in 1959, the son of Ralph Roberts, who founded Comcast, and as a boy sat in on his father's negotiations with banks and cable networks. At 15 he worked at one of his father's other businesses, where on his first day a supervisor told him she did not care whose son he was. He became an All-American squash player and graduated from Wharton in 1981 with a finance degree and investment banking offers. Instead he joined Comcast as a trainee in its Trenton, N.J. cable system, working as a line installer and in branch offices before running operations in his mid-20s. He was named president in 1990, CEO in 2002 and chairman in 2004, and has shared the CEO title with Mike Cavanagh since January 2026.

open_issues: Roberts has been CEO since 2002; tenure.start reflects the co-CEO arrangement per seed (TheWrap gives effective date Jan. 1, 2026).
Timing of operations leadership differs: NYT/Joe Nocera (2015) says head of operations at age 26 (~1985); Wikipedia says promoted to executive vice president in 1987. Career entry uses 1987.

Accounts of his entry differ slightly: NYT says his father resisted bringing him in immediately; Wharton Magazine says his father steered him away from corporate finance to Trenton. Story avoids attributing motive.
Degree field 'Finance' comes from Wharton Magazine ('finance major'); Wikipedia lists a BS without a major.
